description: Idempotently ensures a recurring cron exists (default '30 5 * * *', daily, UTC) that fires check_model_capability_catalog_cron, the EDGE_SINK cron target, looked up by tag (default 'model_capability_guard'). Run it as the ensure_model_capability_guard_schedule entry of the deployment's config/starting_action_definitions.json, which the orchestrator submits after startup completes; nothing installs the cron from a plugin lifecycle method, because scheduling_service does not exist yet at plugin readiness. It resolves the scheduling_service SERVICE binding at call time and raises if it is not available yet. create_cron_schedule is called with a non-empty, system-owned flow_id/session_id in state, because action_factory._enforce_flow_id refuses any action_definition without a flow_id at FIRE time. The cron's action entry is a literal that omits result_processor_kind and targets a verb that declares no result or error processor, so a fire stays terminal. Unlike ensure_host_disk_guard_schedule it does not refuse when this plugin's 'alert_role' config key is unset: the refresh is the point, so the cron is installed anyway and each transition without a target logs at ERROR and reports alert_reason=alert_target_unconfigured. A scheduling_service error response raises rather than being read as 'no existing schedule.' Not discoverable via search (is_discoverable=False): a deploy-time wiring call.
embedding_description: Installs or confirms the daily cron that refreshes the model capability catalog and checks that it is renewing. Idempotent by tag. Installs even when no alert target is configured, because the refresh itself is the purpose. Guards against the EDGE_SINK result_processor_kind headless-cron regression by construction.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: status: one of created, already_present. tag: the schedule tag. cron_expression and schedule_id are set when the cron was just created.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: already_present is the normal outcome on every boot after the first; report it as confirmation, not as a no-op failure.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Distinct from a completed call reporting status=already_present. An error here means the scheduling_service call itself failed, such as a malformed action payload or the scheduling provider being unreachable.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: A raised exception most likely means the verb ran before startup created scheduling_service (it exists only after the init_service_manager step) or the scheduling provider is unresponsive.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Confirm the scheduling_service binding is healthy (for example via a direct get_schedules_by_tag call) before retrying; this verb is marked retryable.
